additional_info.subject: RE: ID0446713-DC/Si-D/NZ-[MP/P3 170000341]Faulty Power Module CRM:02889000534
additional_info.body:
Hey Kiel,
It appears that one charger at Auckland Aiport for Meridian has a defective power module.
Please see below the serial numbers of all the power modules currently being detected in the charger.
The one that is missing, will be the one that is having issues.
We will need on-site attendance to address this.
Under with the 5 electrical safety rules:
Once the charger has been isolated, waiting 10 minutes for de-energisation and cooling of hot components.
Afterwards gaining access to the power modules, verifying the absence of voltage on the AC and DC components.
The technician would then need to go around and account for all the power modules with the matching serial numbers listed here.
The one that is missing is the one we need to draw our attention to.
Checking that the small CAN cable connection is probably connected and that all the connectors into the power module are seated correctly.
If nothing obvious is found, the power module can be replaced, for this reason we would suggest bringing along a spare module.
After installation and re-energisation, please allow us to confirm if the module is again visible and communicating for successful repair.
If we can arrange pick up of the power module from YHI, this is something Lucky has carried out before and can do again.
NCC ID is 303.
Please let me know if you need more details and let me know when this could be arranged.
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer
Email: ferdinand.reisch@siemens.com
www.siemens.com.au/emobility

additional_info.body:
Hey All,
Hope you're doing well.
The defective power module was identified and replaced and all 8 power modules are available and error free.
While onsite our field service technician had a customer approach him, mentioning that the QRcode did not work with the application for authentication.
As the technician was busy, he did not get any further details, but this might be something worth checking up, thought we would let you know.
It was also noted that our technician had to wait 2 hours from the scheduled time to begin the works on the charger, due to the delayed arrival of the other electrical contractor to isolate the charger. In the aim of solving this topic as promptly as possible, potentially short notice was given.
While delays are unforeseeable, this is something that will need to be closing observed for future service works, as this affects case investigation and resolution times, and keeps resources on standby which may impact our operations that will thus need to be accounted for.
We hope you understand and this can be a once-off.
Thanks all and have a good day,
With Kind Regards,
Ferdinand Reisch
Siemens Ltd.
Application Service Engineer

www.siemens.com.au/emobility
